# kenji: the world around the record

Everything here is fictional. It exists so the data has somewhere to come
from: the job explains the discipline, the calendar explains the two blocks,
and the generator draws from these constants so the record and this file agree
by construction.

## Place and work

- Osaka. Japan keeps one UTC offset all year, which is deliberate: every other
  generated record in this corpus crosses a summer-time boundary, so his is
  the one to reach for when a failure might be about the clock rather than the
  numbers.
- Calibration technician. He checks the bench scale against a check mass on
  the first of every month and has never had to adjust it, which is why the
  record carries one instrument and no comparability row.

## The two blocks

- **2030-01-07 to 2030-03-31, the deficit block.** He aims at 480 kcal a day
  under and misses by a variable amount, because a person aiming at a number
  is not a person hitting it. Twelve weeks.
- **2030-04-01 to 2030-06-30, the maintenance block.** He aims at zero. This
  is the experiment: he wants to know how long a record must run before a
  slope this small can be told from no slope at all.

The two blocks are also what give the record a RANGE of weekly balances. A
record held at one steady deficit has a single repeated balance and gives a
correlation nothing to be a correlation of.

## The protocol

Same scale, same time, before eating, after voiding. The protocol slug on
every weigh-in is `morning-fasted-voided` and it never changes for the whole
record - which is not decoration. A protocol change under a weight series
means its two ends are not two readings of one measurand, and the engine
refuses the whole energy question when it sees one.

## After the record ends

He stops weighing his food the same week the block ends and keeps the morning
weigh-in, which is what he did after the last two experiments.
